# Routing gate counts the requesting session's own still-active record: finished turn's next request is refused as `local_concurrency_limit` and exiled remote

## Goal

**As an** operator running several agent sessions against the local Qwen backend, **I want** the local routing concurrency gate to stop counting the requesting session's **own record while it is still flagged `active` after its previous turn has already finished**, **so that** a sequential client's next turn is not spuriously refused with `local_concurrency_limit` and exiled to a remote provider for the rest of the session.

## Problem

`LP-0MW0VH2LB008JSKQ` fixed the *idle*-lease case: `_get_local_concurrency_info(..., session_id=…)` skips the requester's own record when it is an idle lease (`active: false`). It deliberately kept an **`active`** record counting, to preserve gating of a genuinely concurrent second request from the same session.

That leaves a residual race. The record's `active` flag is cleared in `_decrement_local_active_queries` → `_claim_local_dispatch_credit` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, the path that logs `lease_renewed`), which runs on request **teardown** (`router.py` `_cleanup_after_request` → `_decrement_local_active_queries`), not at the point the response reaches its terminal chunk. Measured lag in the incident below: **1.41 s** between `Stream finished` and `lease_renewed`.

A herdr agent re-issues its next turn roughly **145 ms** after the stream ends. In that window `cur_local` includes the requester's own still-`active` record; with `session_slot_pool_size: 2` and one *other* session holding a lease the pool reads 2/2, the gate records `status=local_concurrency_limit`, and because `remote-ok` (the default preference) never queues (`proxy/docs/routing.md:2940`) the request hops immediately to the next remote provider — while the lease gate (`own_has_lease`) would have admitted it.

Sequential-agent turns are the common case, not an edge case: this is one wasted local slot per affected session-turn, and it compounds (see the abandoned-slot consequence below).

### Evidence — 2026-11-18 22:38:47–22:40:15, `herdr-1795041420-110182-25266`

```
22:38:46.138  Stream started: provider=local model=Qwen3 session=…25266 turn=f223ce16
22:38:47.188  local_admission_guard decision=admit … free_slot=true session=herdr-1795041488-125614-6274
22:38:50.808  Stream started: provider=local model=Qwen3 session=…6274 turn=60aa16c5
22:38:52.466  Stream finished … provider=local session=…25266 turn=f223ce16      ← own turn ends
22:38:52.611  priority_routing … preference=remote-ok session=…25266 turn=fab29e5a  (+145 ms)
22:38:52.657  [remote] POST → opencode.ai/zen/go                                   (no routing_check, no guard)
22:38:53.878  lease_renewed session=…25266 timeout=30s                             ← record finally idle
22:39:02.994  Fallback triggered … reason=local_concurrency_limit session=…25266 attempt=1 turn=fab29e5a
```

Occupancy at 22:38:52.611 is exactly 2: `…6274`'s active lease plus `…25266`'s own not-yet-released record. Every other session in the burst (`…5441`, `…2966`, `01a1f0a0-…`, `…67232-890`) hit `local_concurrency_limit` at the same gate in the same seconds, so the second occupant is not an anonymous third party — it is the requester's own finished turn.

Knock-on cost in the same incident: `…25266` was back on local at 22:39:05, stalled behind `…6274`'s single-slot prefill, was evicted by the no-progress watchdog at 22:39:21 (`lease_released … reason=prefill_eta_exceeded elapsed_s=16.6`, `abandoned_slot_recorded slot=1`), and then carried an `843 s` `abandoned_slot_drain` per-session cooldown (`routing_skip_local … reason=abandoned_slot_drain`). So one spurious concurrency refusal preceded a 14-minute local exile for that session.

## Existing state (verified 2026-11-19, HEAD `15db052b2`)

| Piece | Location | Current behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Routing gate | `proxy/proxy/provider.py:16837` | `_local_concurrency_info(config, endpoint=local_endpoint, session_id=_session_id)`; `cur_local >= max_local` → `status=local_concurrency_limit` (`:17031`). Second call site at `:18223` (post-lease-denial retry) uses the same helper. |
| Own-record predicate | `proxy/proxy/provider.py:8175` `_is_own_idle_lease` | Returns `False` when `record["active"]` is truthy — **this is the gap**: only an *inactive* own record is excluded. |
| Per-endpoint counter | `proxy/proxy/provider.py:8201` `_get_local_concurrency_info` | Counts a record when `record["active"]` **or** `expires_at > now`; skips only the own *idle* lease, and only when `session_id` is not `None`. |
| Lease choke point | `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:4649` `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` | `own_has_lease` already admits same-session re-acquisition (`:4782`); record creation sets `"active": True` (`:4918`), overlapping dispatches append a per-dispatch credit token (`:4888`–`:4910`). |
| Credit release / flag clear | `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:3341` `_claim_local_dispatch_credit` (via `:3461` `_decrement_local_active_queries`) | Clears `record["active"] = False` (`:3409`, `:3425`) only when the last outstanding credit is released — i.e. at **teardown**, `lease_renewed` logged at `:3515`. |
| Teardown call site | `proxy/proxy/router.py:890` | `_cleanup_after_request` → `_decrement_local_active_queries(..., dispatch_token=…)`; runs after the response completes, hence the ~1.4 s lag behind the terminal chunk. |
| Other release paths | `router_helpers.py:5737` `_release_unserved_dispatch`, `:6464` `_release_client_disconnect_dispatch` | Already token-scoped and exactly-once; they are not the source of the lag. |
| Docs | `proxy/docs/routing.md:1247`–`:1290` | Occupancy section added by `LP-0MW0VH2LB008JSKQ` states "only an idle lease is excluded; an `active` record always counts" — the rule that must be refined. `:2940` documents that `remote-ok` never queues. |

The race is therefore live on the current tree: nothing marks a record "finished but not yet torn down", so the two gates disagree for the window between the terminal chunk and `_cleanup_after_request`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Red test (the race).** A returning request from a session whose previous local stream has emitted its terminal chunk, where the only thing making `cur_local >= max_local` is that session's own still-`active` record, is **not** refused with `local_concurrency_limit` and is dispatched locally. The test must reproduce the 145 ms ordering (finish, then next request before teardown) and fail on the current tree.
2. **Concurrent work still gated.** Two genuinely overlapping requests from the *same* session (the first still streaming upstream) are still gated — `local_concurrency_limit` / dispatch denial as today. This is the constraint that made `LP-0MW0VH2LB008JSKQ` keep active records counting, and it must not regress.
3. **Anonymous / status paths unchanged.** `session_id=None` callers and the pool-description readers behind `/llama/local/status` and `/llama/local/reserve` exclude nothing, exactly as today.
4. **No new false admission.** A refused-then-admitted dispatch never exceeds `session_slot_pool_size` concurrent local streams; the generating/prefill counters and the dispatch-lease choke point (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch`) remain the authority — the routing gate only stops over-counting, it does not grant capacity.
5. **Measured impact.** Over a ≥24 h window, `local_concurrency_limit` fall-throughs attributable to the requester's own still-`active` record fall to ~0; the measurement is recorded on this item (before/after counts from `proxy.log`, same method as `LP-0MW0VH2LB008JSKQ`).
6. **Docs.** `proxy/docs/routing.md` (the occupancy section added by `LP-0MW0VH2LB008JSKQ`) is extended to state the finished-but-not-yet-released window and how it is handled, including the explicit statement of what still counts as genuine in-flight work; any code comments in `_is_own_idle_lease` / `_get_local_concurrency_info` / `_claim_local_dispatch_credit` that state the old rule are corrected to match.
7. **No behaviour change elsewhere.** Prefill serialisation, admission-guard verdicts, abandoned-slot registry and cooldown scope are untouched.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (via the test skill / `run_tests.py`), including the new tests for AC1–AC4.

## Constraints

- Single source of truth for "is this session's turn still live": do not introduce a second, parallel liveness notion that can drift from `dispatch_credits` / `active`.
- The per-dispatch credit token (`LP-0MVYZEYZY003IQAH`) already distinguishes "this session has ≥1 live dispatch" from "this session's last dispatch is tearing down" — reuse it rather than inventing a timestamp heuristic.
- Exactly-once release semantics (`LP-0MVWF78QK0060TZH` / `LP-0MVYWLBV70018ZZB`) must not be weakened: the routing gate is a **read**, and must stay read-only.
- No change to the `session_id=None` contract (AC3); `/llama/local/status` must keep reporting engine-truth occupancy.
- `remote-ok` still never queues — this item removes a false refusal, it does not add waiting.

## Desired change

The routing concurrency gate stops counting the requesting session's own record in the finished-but-not-yet-released window, while still counting it while any dispatch of that session is genuinely in flight — so a sequential client's next turn is admitted locally and a concurrent second request is gated as today.

Candidate mechanisms (decide in the plan; AC2 is the binding constraint; prefer the smallest change):

- clear the record's `active` flag (or set an explicit `finished`/`streaming: false` marker) when the response reaches its terminal chunk, before teardown bookkeeping;
- treat an `active` own record with **no** live in-flight upstream dispatch as non-occupancy for that session (per-dispatch live-work attribution, cf. `LP-0MVZ3V8J1006YGFN`);
- extend `_is_own_idle_lease` into an own-record predicate keyed on an explicit finished/streaming state rather than on the teardown timestamp.

## Key Files (verified 2026-11-19)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_is_own_idle_lease` (`:8175`, the predicate to extend), `_get_local_concurrency_info` (`:8201`), `_local_concurrency_info` wrapper (`:8120`), gate sites `:16837` and `:18223`, `status=local_concurrency_limit` attempt record (`:17031`).
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (`:4649`, `own_has_lease` at `:4782`, record creation `active: True` at `:4918`, credit append `:4888`–`:4910`), `_claim_local_dispatch_credit` (`:3341`), `_decrement_local_active_queries` (`:3461`, `lease_renewed` at `:3515`), `_release_unserved_dispatch` (`:5737`), `_release_client_disconnect_dispatch` (`:6464`).
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `_cleanup_after_request` teardown decrement (`:890`), the site that runs ~1.4 s after the terminal chunk.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — occupancy section `:1247`–`:1290`; `remote-ok` never queues `:2940`.
- `proxy/tests/` — the `LP-0MW0VH2LB008JSKQ` own-lease tests (the pattern to follow for AC1/AC2) and the dispatch-credit tests from `LP-0MVYWLBV70018ZZB`; locate by `rg -n "_is_own_idle_lease|own_has_lease|dispatch_credits" proxy/tests`.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `session_slot_pool_size`, `local_dispatch_lease_timeout_seconds` (read-only context for the repro).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (AC2 regression).** A predicate that keys on "response finished" alone can be fooled by a stream that finishes early (client disconnect mid-stream, watchdog eviction): the record could be marked finished while upstream work is still winding down, admitting a third concurrent stream. Mitigation: key on the live dispatch-credit set, not on a response-side flag alone.
- **Risk (scope creep).** The incident also exposed the `enforced=false` `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` admit path and the umbrella `no_progress_watchdog` reason; both are explicitly out of scope and stay as linked items.
- **Risk (measurement ambiguity).** Post-fix the same log line can still appear for genuine contention, so AC5 must classify by "own record only" occupancy, not by the raw count.
- **Assumption:** the ~1.4 s teardown lag is inherent to the ASGI teardown path (not a bug to fix here); the gate must tolerate it rather than the teardown being accelerated.
- **Assumption:** the incident evidence (07:38Z trace above) is representative of agent turn cadence (~145 ms gap), so a repro at that ordering is realistic.

## Also observed (out of scope here)

- The `enforced=false` `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` admit path can dispatch into a prefill-starved pool and end in watchdog eviction plus a per-session `abandoned_slot_drain` cooldown. Tracked separately if raised.
- `local_eviction_after_acceptance` still reports the umbrella reason `no_progress_watchdog` (see `LP-0MWKQJHSM000CI6W`).

## Related work

- **LP-0MW0VH2LB008JSKQ** — *Routing concurrency gate counts the requesting session's own idle lease, pushing returning sessions remote* (completed). Direct predecessor: fixed the idle-lease case and deliberately left `active` records counting. This item is its residual window.
- **LP-0MVZ3V8J1006YGFN** — *Scope dispatch teardown to its own dispatch (per-dispatch live-work attribution)* (completed). Supplies the per-dispatch `dispatch_credits` / `dispatch_token` machinery the fix should reuse.
- **LP-0MVYWLBV70018ZZB** — *[impl] AC3+AC8: exactly-once counter decrement on every release path* (completed). Parent `LP-0MVWF78QK0060TZH`; defines the exactly-once release invariant the routing gate must not perturb.
- **LP-0MVYZEYZY003IQAH** — *Fix status builder live-work attribution during prefill* (open, plan_complete). Adjacent "which dispatch is live" question, on the status surface rather than the routing gate; shares the same attribution seam.
- **LP-0MVK16GME007EYUW** — *Idle admission is gated by foreign idle local leases* (completed). The mirror-image case (someone *else*'s idle lease), fixed by the same family of occupancy rules.
- **LP-0MWNEUJOH000KMG9** — sibling raised from the same incident: the 843 s `abandoned_slot_drain` deferral armed by the no-progress eviction.
- **LP-0MWKQJHSM000CI6W** — umbrella `no_progress_watchdog` eviction reason.
- Docs: `proxy/docs/routing.md` §"Routing occupancy counts other sessions, not your own lease" (`:1247`), `:2940` (remote-ok never queues).

## Impact

Agents get their next local turn served by Qwen instead of being silently bounced to a paid remote provider whenever they come back within about a second of their own previous turn finishing.

---

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview was required: the item arrived from live incident triage with a complete problem statement, seven testable acceptance criteria and an evidence trace, so the intake pass was verification-only (repo research against HEAD `15db052b2`). The questions below were resolved by agent research and are recorded for auditability.

- Q: "Is the residual race still present on the current tree, or was it closed as a side-effect of `LP-0MW0VH2LB008JSKQ`?" — Answer (agent research): still present. `_is_own_idle_lease` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:8175`) returns `False` whenever `record["active"]` is truthy, and `active` is only cleared in `_claim_local_dispatch_credit` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:3409`) on teardown (`router.py:890`). Source: code read at HEAD `15db052b2`.
- Q: "Does any existing mechanism already distinguish 'this session's dispatch finished' from 'this session's dispatch is live'?" — Answer (agent research): yes, partially — per-dispatch credit tokens (`dispatch_credits` / `dispatch_token`, `LP-0MVYZEYZY003IQAH`) record which dispatches are outstanding on a record, but the routing gate does not consult them; it only reads the boolean `active`. Source: `router_helpers.py:4888`–`:4920`, `:3385`–`:3425`.
- Q: "Would excluding the own record unconditionally break same-session concurrency gating (the constraint behind `LP-0MW0VH2LB008JSKQ`)?" — Answer (agent research): yes, which is why AC2 exists; the predicate must stay keyed on live outstanding dispatches, not on "the response finished". Source: `LP-0MW0VH2LB008JSKQ` description and `proxy/docs/routing.md:1281`.
- Q: "Is this a duplicate of any open item?" — Answer (agent research): no. Duplicate check performed with `wl search "local_concurrency_limit"`, `wl search "finished turn still active record"` and `wl search "own record active finished teardown lease"`: no open item covers this window. `LP-0MVYZEYZY003IQAH` (open) covers status-surface live-work attribution during prefill; `LP-0MVK16GME007EYUW` (completed) covered *foreign* idle leases. Recorded as related work, not duplicates.
- Q: "Does the routing gate's own count drive capacity, or only admission?" — Answer (agent research): admission only. `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (`router_helpers.py:4649`) remains the choke point and `available_slots`/`total_slots` come from llama-server `/slots`, so AC4's "no new false admission" holds as long as the routing gate stays a read. Source: `proxy/docs/routing.md:1286`–`:1300`.
- Q: "Is the ~1.4 s teardown lag itself in scope?" — Answer (agent research / scope decision): no. The gate must tolerate the lag; accelerating teardown would touch the exactly-once release invariant. Source: incident trace (`Stream finished` 22:38:52.466 → `lease_renewed` 22:38:53.878) and `LP-0MVYWLBV70018ZZB`.

No open questions for the producer: AC2 fixes the design constraint, and the mechanism choice is deliberately left to the plan stage.

# Identify and eliminate the non-proxy client that polls the router `/slots` model-less

**discovered-from:LP-0MVU8003X0018WT8** (AC4 measurement, 2026-11-19)

## Summary

While measuring the AC4 window, a **non-proxy local client** was found opening short-lived loopback connections to the llama-server router (`127.0.0.1:8080`) whose `GET /slots` requests are answered **HTTP 400**. Because llama.cpp logs neither the query string nor a timestamp on that line, the client's identity cannot be recovered from `llama-server.log`, so it is un-attributed today — and it keeps the router-responder `router:400` count non-zero, masking the signal the AC4/AC1 verification depends on.

## Evidence (2026-11-19)

- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` responder split over the two window files: `router:400 = 1,008` (`llama-server.log-2026-11-19`, 2026-11-18) + `388` (`llama-server.log`, 2026-11-19; 2 of them this session's own probes) with `router:500 = 0` and `child:200 = 99,865`.
- The proxy cannot be the producer: its only model-less `/slots` URL is completed with `?model=` (`proxy/proxy/observability.py:2196-2202`), and `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="http_400"}` has **no series at any point in the window** (Prometheus `count by (reason)` returns only `reason="timeout"`).
- Live capture 2026-11-19T15:27–15:31Z: `ss`/`/proc/net/tcp` sampling recorded multiple short-lived ESTABLISHED connections `127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>` → `127.0.0.1:8080` owned by uid 1000, in bursts of 3–16 requests, while the bare-400 count rose 371 → 388. `ss -p` could not resolve the owning pid at sampling resolution, and `sudo` is unavailable in the agent session, so root-owned/podman-host-network ownership was neither confirmed nor excluded.
- Live reproduction of the two permitted producer classes: bare `GET /slots` → 400; `GET /slots?model=does-not-exist` → 400 (identical log line shape).

## Desired outcome

1. **Identify** the client: candidates are a script/cron/timer, an agent-runbook command (`proxy/docs/runbook-5xx.md:52` documents a bare `curl -s http://localhost:8080/slots`, which *provokes* a 400 by design), `scripts/verify_slots_observability.py`'s deliberate bare probe, or a containerised monitor on host networking. Use a root-capable capture (e.g. `ss -tnp` as root, `bpftrace`/`execsnoop`, or `conntrack -E`) to bind the connection to a pid and command line.
2. **Decide** per call site: keep it if it is an intentional negative probe (then exclude it from the triage count / document it), or route it to `?model=<resolved id>` / stop polling if it is incidental.
3. **Document** the outcome in `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` (router vs child responder split, attribution rule) and update the parent item's AC1 re-check ("no non-proxy client polls the router `/slots` directly" — currently does not hold).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The client is named by pid + command line (or explicitly proven to be root/container-owned) with the capture transcript recorded as a comment.
- [ ] Each call site is either fixed (`?model=` / stop polling) or documented as an intentional negative probe that the triage tooling counts separately.
- [ ] `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` records the finding and how to read it in the responder split.
- [ ] Re-measurement after the fix shows `router:400` attributable to zero unexplained events over a fresh window.

## Key Files

- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py`
- `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`
- `proxy/docs/runbook-5xx.md`
- `scripts/verify_slots_observability.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`

# Goal

As the producer, I want one recorded decision on what `slots_stale < 5 %` **means** — the delivered
300 s "unusably old" bound, the plan's 2 s freshness value, or both as separate statements — so the
number cannot be quoted as evidence of freshness when it is not.

# Why (the measured ambiguity)

The post-fix 24 h window (`2026-11-18T10:25Z → 2026-11-19T10:25Z`, record
`docs/dev/slots-stale-postfix-window-2026-11-18-to-19.md`) passes the target on the delivered
definition and fails it by ×6.3 on the plan's candidate:

| Definition | Reading | Target |
|---|---|---|
| age > 300 s ceiling (delivered, `max(120, 10 × 30 s cadence)`) | **4.88 %** | < 5 % → **met** |
| age > 2 s (plan Q3 candidate) | **31.60 %** of datable polls | < 5 % → **missed** |
| age p50 / p90 / p99 / max | 0.73 s / 35.14 s / 187.73 s / 424.20 s | — |

81.3 % of the over-2 s polls carry `capacity_hint=prefill_bound`, i.e. the snapshot ages because the
backend is blocked in prefill; no read-path change removes that. The choice is therefore a contract
choice, not a defect fix, and it is the producer's (parent AC2 second branch).

# Options (the decision, not a preference)

1. **Keep 300 s**, and describe `slots_stale` everywhere as an *unusably-old* bound — never as freshness.
2. **Tighten** to a stated value (2 s candidate) with its own re-baselined target, accepting ~32 % today.
3. **Two-tier**: keep `slots_stale` at 300 s (safety bound) and add a separate freshness SLO on
   `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` (candidate 2 s) with its own threshold and report line.

# Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Decision recorded.** This item carries the producer's choice (one of the three options, or
  an explicit alternative) with its rationale and the date.
- **AC2 — Definition written down.** The chosen definition is applied to every place that quotes the
  target: the parent's AC2 text, `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, and any tracker/doc
  that states `< 5 %` (grep the literal).
- **AC3 — Change is pinned if the threshold moves.** Any ceiling/threshold change ships with a
  relabelling/consistency test (same discipline as LP-0MWM0CSDL008RB1E AC3), and the report labels
  every pre/post figure by the definition that produced it.
- **AC4 — Baselines carried.** The decision note carries the comparable figures side by side:
  2026-10-29 29.59 % and 2026-11-01/02 40.48 % and 2026-11-16/17 18.03 % (all **pre-definition-change**,
  cache-fallback semantics), plus 2026-11-18/19 4.88 % at 300 s and 31.60 % at 2 s (age semantics).
- **AC5 — Downstream informed.** LP-0MWM0CSDL008RB1E (gate redesign) and LP-0MWRXGPO3004GXD7
  (nightly reporting) are pointed at the decision so neither re-litigates it.

# Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` (`local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds`, cadence-derived default)
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`
- `docs/dev/slots-stale-postfix-window-2026-11-18-to-19.md` + `.json`
- `scripts/slots_snapshot_age_distribution.py`

## Impact

Every future `slots_stale` claim states what it measured, so a passing target can no longer be
mistaken for a freshness guarantee.
